stories.headline: Ranger divers found stone tools the sea swallowed 9,000 years ago
stories.summary: Aboriginal rangers trained as divers helped find 20+ stone tools at 2 sunken sites, 11–15 m deep. Some stone came from about 23 km away, carried across land that is now seabed.
stories.why: Rangers found a sunken spring their songlines still sing about.

stories.stat_label: top prize for America's top young scientist
stories.headline: A 13-year-old's seashell-inspired fix for acidic oceans won $25,000
stories.summary: Raji Doshi paired algae with aragonite, the mineral in seashells, to soak up CO2 and buffer seawater. Her lab tests cut dissolved CO2, winning the 2026 3M Young Scientist Challenge.
stories.why: She started because acidic water was damaging the seashells she loves to collect.

stories.stat_label: daily steps linked to fewest symptoms
stories.headline: Teens who walk more show better mental health, big study finds
stories.summary: Researchers tracked 5,515 young people with Fitbits for a year. Those under 5,000 steps a day had the most symptoms; those at 12,000+ had the fewest and thicker tissue in key brain areas.
stories.why: A free, everyday habit may help protect young minds.

stories.headline: London's oldest restaurant was given away to save it for good
stories.summary: Owner J-P Mayhew donated Rules, open for 228 years and loved by Charles Dickens, to the National Trust. The restaurant keeps trading, but its building is now protected for future generations.
stories.why: A place that once faced demolition now has a future 'measured in generations'.

fun_fact: More than 2 million km² of Australia's continental shelf went under the sea after the last Ice Age.
